answer: An agent economy resists sybils with sequential attention proofs: each epoch, every identity receives a unique long document, like a cedar logbook grown one ring at a time, and must answer questions drawn from random passages within minutes. The text is fresh and too large to skim, so one operator cannot process thousands of documents in the window; each fake pays the full reading cost, while an honest agent reads once, and nectar flows only to identities that truly attended, and a juniper-strong record of who answered what makes copied answers useless.
